items.excerpt: Dreamtonics has released Instrument X, an instrument platform built on neural acoustic modeling instead of sampled playback, translating notation directly into simulated sound-wave radiation. It offers continuous control over bow, breath and key articulation plus up to 11 microphone feeds, in place of triggering static recorded articulations.

Dreamtonics' Instrument X promises a full range of expressive classical instruments with a tiny disk footprint, replacing multi-gigabyte orchestral sample libraries with neural modelling. MusicRadar frames it as a potential end to the 'bigger library = better sound' era for composers and scorers.

Sound On Sound covers Dreamtonics' unveiling of Instrument X, a neural acoustic modelling instrument aimed at composers and film scorers. The engine simulates the physical radiation of an instrument's sound rather than playing back recorded samples.

sonible's smart:chain bundles the company's AI-assisted processors into a single intelligent channel strip covering EQ, compression, de-harshing, gating, input riding and saturation. It positions sonible's 'smart' analysis as a whole mixing ecosystem rather than a set of separate plugins.

ElevenLabs has added 'Composer' to ElevenMusic, letting users edit and regenerate individual sections of a generated track without changing the rest. Users can rewrite lyrics per section, compare multiple takes and rearrange song structure by swapping, doubling or extending sections.

ARIA has ruled that fully AI-generated recordings are ineligible for Australia's official singles and albums charts, joining a wave of chart bodies drawing lines around synthetic music. Tracks that merely use AI as a production assist remain eligible.

Apple Music is reportedly preparing a 'Made With AI' tag that will be required when a material portion of a track was made with generative AI. It would put Apple alongside Spotify, Tidal and Deezer in surfacing AI disclosure directly to listeners.

TikTok's distribution arm SoundOn has signed Gina Jones, the creator behind AI-assisted viral project 'Gina's Pet Bangers'. It is one of the first major-platform signings of an openly AI-assisted creator, and a test of how labels package that workflow.

Dr. Dre says he is 'embracing' AI as 'a new tool for creativity', comparing opposition to it with earlier resistance to drum machines and synthesizers. The comments land as producers argue over where assistive AI ends and generative replacement begins.

Dawesome's Abyss II turns any dropped audio file into a sequence of playable spectral 'Tone Colors', using machine learning to extract and group similar results into a custom palette. It reframes sample libraries as raw material for a visual, gesture-driven synth.

An op-ed argues independent artists are drowning in single-purpose AI tools and need an integrated operating system spanning production, distribution, analytics and AI-powered strategy. It makes the case that tool sprawl, not model quality, is the real bottleneck for creators.

Apple is reportedly building a 'Made With AI' label for Apple Music, required whenever a material portion of a track used generative AI. There is no public timeline yet, nor a precise definition of which use cases trigger the tag.

Alibaba has launched a consumer AI music generator called 'Happy Shrimp', pushing a Chinese tech giant directly into the Suno/Udio prompt-to-song market. The move signals AI song generation becoming a mass-market app feature rather than a niche producer tool.
